    Has there ever been a 16-1 upset?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, there have been
    two16-seed over 1-seed upsets in the men's NCAA tournament since the field expanded in 1985    . 
    • 2018: UMBC (University of Maryland, Baltimore County) defeated #1 Virginia 74-54.
    • 2023: FDU (Fairleigh Dickinson) defeated #1 Purdue 63-58.
      These remain the only times a 16-seed has beaten a 1-seed.       
    Key Facts about 16-1 Upsets: 
    • Historic Impact: UMBC became the first No. 16 seed to ever beat a No. 1 in 2018.
    • FDU vs. Purdue: FDU, the shortest team in the tournament, defeated a Purdue team that was the tallest, notes
      WKYC.
    • Dominance: Before these, No. 1 seeds had dominated with a 162-2 all-time record against 16 seeds, according to NCAA.com.
    • Frequency: 16-seeds have a 1.25% winning percentage against 1-seeds.
